findings.problem: Says Baco Blanc was due to go under an EU ban on hybrid vines. The planned removal was a French appellation decision (out of Armagnac by 2010), reversed in 2005; EU hybrid rules govern PDO wine, not spirits.
findings.fix: Now says French rules once ordered it out of Armagnac by 2010 and the order was reversed in 2005.
findings.source: Armagnac appellation history: the INAO phase-out set in the 1990s and lifted in 2005.

findings.stemStart: Sonora makes an agave spirit with a Mexican
findings.problem: Says bacanora was outlawed in Mexico for most of the twentieth century. The ban was the state of Sonora's own, from 1915 to 1992, not a national one.
findings.fix: Now says it was outlawed in Sonora itself from 1915 until 1992.
findings.source: Bacanora history: Sonora's state prohibition of 1915, lifted in 1992 ahead of the 2000 denomination.

findings.stemStart: Absinthe's early twentieth-century ban was blamed on a
findings.problem: Gives the EU thujone cap as 35 mg per litre in bitter spirits. That is the old directive's wording; the current flavourings regulation sets 35 mg per kilogram for drinks made from Artemisia species.
findings.fix: Now: thirty-five milligrams per kilogram in drinks made from Artemisia.
findings.source: Regulation (EC) 1334/2008, Annex III Part B (thujone: 35 mg/kg in alcoholic drinks made from Artemisia).

findings.stemStart: Vermouth is a wine before it is anything
findings.problem: Says the band runs to twenty-two percent and that above it the drink becomes a bitter liqueur. The aromatised wine band is 14.5 to less than 22 percent; below it the product is an aromatised wine-based drink and at 22 or more it simply fails the definition, so it does not become a bitter liqueur.
findings.fix: Now: just under twenty-two percent; below the floor it drops into the aromatised wine-based drinks; at twenty-two or more it is no longer an aromatised wine.
findings.source: Regulation (EU) 251/2014, Annex II (aromatised wine 14.5 to under 22 percent; aromatised wine-based drinks 4.5 to under 14.5 percent).

findings.stemStart: One style of vermouth carries a geographical indication
findings.problem: Says the Superiore tier adds that the Artemisia be grown in Piedmont. Piedmontese Artemisia is required of all Vermouth di Torino; Superiore adds at least 17 percent, at least half Piedmontese wine and other herbs grown or gathered in Piedmont. Also dropped an unsupported causal claim that this is why the bitters trade grew up in Turin (much of it grew up in Milan).
findings.fix: Rewrote the first sentence to the disciplinare's split between the base and Superiore tiers, and ended on the late eighteenth-century start in Turin.
findings.source: Vermouth di Torino disciplinare (DM 22 March 2017), confirmed by one web search (Gambero Rosso and trade summaries).

findings.problem: States as fact that the Sazerac began on Cognac and moved to rye after phylloxera. That is a popular tradition that cocktail historians dispute, not documented history.
findings.fix: Now gives the name's Cognac-brand origin and calls the brandy-to-rye switch a tradition rather than a documented fact.
findings.source: Cocktail history: the switch rests on later retellings; early records do not settle which spirit came first.

findings.stemStart: Italy will not consider a wine for its
findings.problem: Keyed Ten years. Law 238/2016, art. 33(1), as amended by Decree-Law 76/2020 (art. 43-ter), reserves DOCG for wines that have held DOC for at least seven years. Ten years was the earlier figure (Legislative Decree 61/2010).
findings.fix: Rekeyed ans to Seven years. Replaced the accept list with the same set of forms for seven (digits, words, at least, minimum, as a DOC, at DOC level, bare 7 and seven), ex=True kept. Exp now says seven years and notes that older books give ten. Probed: ten years, less than seven years, seven years in bottle and five years all grade wrong.
findings.source: Legge 238/2016 art. 33 c.1, as amended by DL 76/2020 art. 43-ter (one web search; the reproduced amending text sets da almeno sette anni).

findings.problem: Says a wine short of 120 g/L goes out as late harvest or sweet szamorodni instead. Szamorodni is by definition a whole-bunch wine, not a wine of picked aszu berries macerated in base, so it cannot catch a failed Aszu. The README notes this routing as a past cross-module hazard.
findings.fix: Cut the routing clause: a wine short of the figure cannot be sold as Aszu at all, so the reform tightened the name.
findings.source: Tokaj product specification: szamorodni is made from bunches picked with their botrytised berries, never separated; Aszu is a maceration of picked aszu berries.
